name: @cloudsforge/wallet-extension
description: CloudsForge's self-custody wallet for Chrome, Firefox, Opera and Edge — EIP-1193, EIP-6963, EIP-3085/3326 over MV3.
//core: @cloudsforge/hearth-wallet-core is consumed from the sibling checkout because it is not published yet — the same arrangement micro-hub-web has with @cloudsforge/ui, and it becomes '^1.0.0' the day the core is published with nothing else here changing. `link:` rather than `file:` is deliberate: link: symlinks the working tree so a fix in the signing core is visible here immediately, whereas pnpm PACKS a file: directory and the packed copy goes stale the moment the core is touched. Three clients depending on divergent copies of a signer is the worst failure this design can have (25-wallet-clients.md §3), and a stale pack is exactly how that starts.
//ui: There is no @cloudsforge/ui dependency, and that is a decision rather than an oversight. The design system is PRIVATE, so consuming it would put a secrets.ESTATE_READ_TOKEN checkout in front of every CI run of a wallet that is otherwise entirely public and self-contained; its components are laid out for 1200px app chrome rather than a 360px popup; and it needs a test loader to survive the second React realpath that `link:` creates. The brand is carried instead by src/ui/tokens.css, whose values are copied from micro-ui's tokens.css and cited line by line there.

scripts.//test:e2e: --test-concurrency=1 because each file launches its own Chromium with its own user-data directory and its own unpacked extension; run in parallel they contend for the same Hearth node's nonces and for the machine's memory. The timeout is generous because these tests wait on real block times, a real 600,000-iteration PBKDF2 unlock, and a real service-worker restart — none of which are worth making flaky to save a minute. 600s rather than 180s since phase 5, and the arithmetic matters: ForesightMarket refuses to resolve a market that is still open (:239) — the rule that stops a resolver staking on the answer it is about to write — so the claim test must wait for a real market to reach its close time. The window is 240 CHAIN seconds, and the chain clock runs at about 0.88x wall time on this estate, so waiting it out costs roughly 270s of wall time MINUS whatever the earlier tests already spent. The faster the machine, the longer that wait: on a slow node the stake test eats most of the window, on a fast one almost none of it. 600s covers the fast case with room, and a smaller number would have failed on fast machines while passing on slow ones — the worst way round.
scripts.//templates:check: Fails when src/background/templates.generated.ts is not what micro-mint's committed artefacts produce. test/templates.test.ts asserts the same thing in-process; this is the form a human runs.
scripts.check: pnpm typecheck && pnpm build:all && pnpm test
